newsitem.title: USA: U.N. okays 41st Iraq oil contract for 900,000 bbls.
newsitem.headline: U.N. okays 41st Iraq oil contract for 900,000 bbls.

text.p: United Nations' overseers approved the 41st Iraqi oil contract under the three month old oil-for-food accord, a U.N. official said on Tuesday.
The latest contract is for 900,000 barrels of Iraqi crude to be lifted on a term basis.
There were no new contracts pending, though a contract recently turned back on a procedural fault may be resubmitted in the near future, the official said.
No further details were available on the latest contract.
On Monday, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) newsletter reported that Iraq had signed five new term crude contracts and one spot sale for the second 90-day period of the oil deal.
U.N. officials and Western diplomats could not immediately confirm the MEES report.

The new term contracts were reportedly with India's Indian Oil Corp for 40,000 barrels per day (bpd), Cyprus for 8,800 bpd, Turkey's Delta for 10,000 bpd, Erden for 10,000 bpd and Japan's Cosmo Oil Corp for 10,000 bpd.
MEES said one spot deal for 1.7 million barrels, or 19,000 bpd had also been signed with France's Elf Aquitaine.
The 41st contract would bring oil volumes for all contracts approved to slightly under 113 million barrels.

Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion of crude oil for six months, mainly to buy food and aid for civilians suffering from the effects of broad sanctions imposed after Iraq invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
